beats.narration_text: Bonjour. This is Liam, in for Bear. A model that looks right in Blender can still arrive in a game wrong. So the real question isn't how it looks. It's what the game actually received.

beats.act: terms
beats.narration_text: Six terms. A mesh is the points and faces that make a shape. A collider is an invisible shape the physics engine tests against. A bounding box is the smallest upright box around a shape. G L T F is a file format for three-D models. Headless means running a program with no window. And M C P, the Model Context Protocol, is a standard that lets an agent call another program's tools.

an invisible shape the physics engine tests against
the smallest upright box around a shape
a file format for 3D models; distances in metres, Y is up
running a program with no window

beats.act: III · Metres, Axes and Applied Scale
beats.narration_text: Start with size. In Blender's default scene, one unit is one metre. The glTF format says every linear distance is in metres. And Godot says one unit in three-D is one metre.

shot.visual_intent: Act title top-left. The pipeline is on stage from the start: Blender's real icon, a drawn glTF file, Godot's real icon, each named. A dimension bar of the same length draws under each, labelled '1 unit = 1 m', 'all in metres', '1 unit = 1 m'.
shot.motion_claim: One and the same bar lands under three different tools, on the three sentences that state it.

lecture.why: The claim is that the SAME measure holds in three places; an identical bar drawn three times shows it, three ruler icons would only name it. Tools are shown as themselves (real app icons).

beats.act: III · Metres, Axes and Applied Scale

beats.act: III · Metres, Axes and Applied Scale
beats.narration_text: Now direction. Blender is right-handed, with Z pointing up. The glTF format and Godot are also right-handed, but with Y pointing up. Somebody has to turn the world on the way in.

beats.act: verdict
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A model that looks right can arrive wrong, so check the numbers. A script run leaves a file you can diff, so set the exit code flag.
